transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Vice President J.D. Vance is accusing Microsoft of fraud.
In a news conference today, Vance announced the Trump administration would suspend the
tech giant from a program to apply for green cards for employees who come to the United
States to live and work on an H-1B visa.
Vance alleges the company, co-founded by Bill Gates, replaced every laid-off worker with
"one and a half foreign indentured servants."
Microsoft is a financial supporter of NPR.
Hurricane Isaias could make landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday/early Saturday,
and Piersville Chapel reports it's the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026.
It's been more than 100 years since the Atlantic area got its first hurricane of the season
this late, but now officials are urging people to finish preparing today for Hurricane Isaias.
Forecasters believe Isaias will grow into a strong Category 2 hurricane before hitting
the coast.
Parts of Mississippi, Alabama, and the Florida Panhandle are under alert for dangerous winds
and a storm surge that could reach 5 to 7 feet in some areas.
The National Hurricane Center says Isaias will move quickly after making landfall, bringing
heavy rain and strong wind far inland over the weekend.
Bill Chappell, NPR News.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says Russia's war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate
and that the Trump administration is committed to working toward a settlement.
NPR's Michelle Kellerman reports Rubio stops short of criticizing Russia for killing civilians
in Ukraine.
Secretary Rubio says stalemates are dangerous.
He says either the two sides need to give up something in order to get to a negotiated
peace or the conflict will escalate.
"That could quickly turn what is a war between two countries into a much broader and far
more dangerous regional conflict.
So I think and I hope that the risk of escalation is one of the things that will bring both
sides to the table and willing to negotiate a settlement to this war."
He was speaking in Portugal on his way home from a trip to three NATO countries.
Portugal's foreign minister says Russia has been more and more aggressive in its attacks
on civilians and he calls that a big danger for the world.
Michelle Kellerman, NPR News, the State Department.
President Trump returned to Texas last night for the third time in a month to stump for
Republican congressional candidates as the GOP faces the prospect of losing control of
Congress in next month's elections.
Trump spoke at a packed frame in Coliseum in San Antonio.
A small group of protesters interrupted his speech.
Some were led away by police.
Before the event, Trump told White House reporters that he had no regrets about endorsing Republican
Senate nominee Ken Paxton, following reports of an audio leak blaming Paxton's campaign
struggles on Trump's war with Iran and resulting high gas prices in the United States.
Recent polls suggest Paxton is trailing Democratic State Representative James Talarico.
This is NPR News.
After nearly eight months in space, the four members of NASA's Crew-12 mission are back
home.
Their SpaceX Crew Dragon capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of
Los Angeles a short time ago.
The two NASA astronauts, one from the European Space Agency and a Russian cosmonaut, spent
235 days aboard the International Space Station.
Warren's British police obtained that led to the search and seizure of former Prince
Andrew's property earlier this year are now invalidated today, a Lenin judge said police
agree the warrants should not have been issued in the first place.
Police obtained the warrants as part of their investigation into Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's
connection to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
The former prince, who was stripped of his title last year in the midst of the scandal,
was arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office.
Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering software developer who wrote code for the Apollo moon lander,
has died at the age of 90, and Piers Jeff Brumfield has more.
Hamilton was born in Indiana and studied mathematics in college.
She became involved in the Apollo program through MIT and eventually was put in charge
of the onboard flight software.
To describe the work, Hamilton coined the term software engineer.
Here she is in 2017.
The engineers thought it was funny, there's Margaret again with her software engineering.
But it stuck.
Hamilton received many awards throughout her career, including the Presidential Medal of
Freedom from Barack Obama in 2016.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News, in Washington.

Hurricane Isaias could make landfall on northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday
Secretary of State Rubio says Russia's war in Ukraine is at dangerous stalemate
President Trump returns to Texas to campaign for Republican congressional candidates in San Antonio
NASA's Crew-12 mission returns to Earth after nearly eight months aboard space station
British court invalidates warrants used to search Prince Andrew's property in Epstein investigation
Margaret Hamilton, pioneering software developer for Apollo moon lander, dies at age ninety
